result.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
result.summary: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 FunCAD-Harness 与 FunCADBench，让 LLM agent 根据欠规格的功能需求构建并迭代修改 CAD 机构，借助物理仿真生成的候选特定测试暴露视觉检查不可见的机械失效，并据此提升功能成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「外观合理但功能失效」的诊断与「用候选特定测试＋仿真反馈驱动迭代修改」的验证循环，可能为 LVR 中检验 latent 状态是否真正承载任务必要信息、何时停止并补充证据提供评价层面的启发；但领域为 CAD 机构合成，与视觉或多模态推理的联系需进一步核查。
